summary: Defect density rises with dose from dose 1 to dose 3, then the spectrum of dose 4 shows that the D/G ratio is no longer a usable measure. Lorentzian fits give I_D/I_G (peak heights) of 0.250 ± 0.017, 0.570 ± 0.017, 1.19 ± 0.03 and 0.57 ± 0.03 for doses 1–4. Using the stage-1 graphene relation of Cançado et al. (Nano Lett. 2011) at 532 nm, the mean defect distance L_D falls from about 24 nm to 16 nm to 11 nm, and the defect density n_D rises from about 5.5e10 to 1.3e11 to 2.6e11 cm⁻² (coefficient uncertainty ±28%). Dose 4 is past the D/G maximum: the G band is ~3.3× wider, the D band ~4× wider, G is up-shifted by ~11 cm⁻¹, and 2D is essentially gone. This is the amorphization (stage-2) signature, so the L_D formula does not apply there and dose 4 has the most disorder even though its D/G is lower than dose 3. The absolute densities are calibration-dependent; the trend across doses 1–3 is robust across window and baseline choices (spread ≤ 0.004 in I_D/I_G).

observations.finding: I_D/I_G (peak heights from Lorentzian fits, D and G with linear baseline) rises from 0.250 to 0.570 to 1.19 across doses 1–3 (about ×2.3 then ×2.1 per step), then falls to 0.57 at dose 4.
observations.evidence: Fit table (primary window): D_H = 703±46, 2046±52, 2971±37, 1833±49 counts; G_H = 2808±48, 3593±56, 2492±43, 3201±168 counts. Window/baseline variants (narrowD, quadratic baseline) change I_D/I_G by ≤0.004. Area-based ratio gives 0.27, 0.61, 1.26, 0.74, the same trend.

observations.finding: Stage-1 defect spacing and density at 532 nm: L_D ≈ 24, 16 and 11 nm and n_D ≈ 5.5e10, 1.3e11 and 2.6e11 cm⁻² for doses 1–3, using L_D² = 1.8e-9·λ⁴/(I_D/I_G) (λ in nm) and n_D = 1/(πL_D²) = 1.8e22·(I_D/I_G)/λ⁴. The coefficient 1.8±0.5 gives an L_D range of about ±14% and an n_D range of ×0.72–1.28.
observations.evidence: λ⁴ = 8.01e10 nm⁴ at 532 nm, so the prefactor is 144 nm². I_D/I_G = 0.250, 0.570, 1.192 gives L_D² = 577, 253, 121 nm². Dose 4 is not computed because the relation is invalid there.
observations.source: Cançado et al., Nano Lett. 11, 3190 (2011), stage-1 relation for L_D and n_D (coefficient as recalled, not checked against the paper)

observations.finding: Dose 4 is in the amorphization regime: I_D/I_G is no longer a monotonic measure of defect density, even though disorder indicators are highest there.
observations.evidence: G FWHM 13.8 → 45.0 cm⁻¹ (×3.3); D FWHM 14.7 → 58.4 cm⁻¹ (×4); G position 1580.4 → 1591.4 cm⁻¹; I_2D/I_G 3.0 (doses 1–3) → 0.07–0.19 (dose 4, 2D not resolved, 2D/Si 0.036 vs ~1.5 earlier). Dose-4 2D fit variants give 236, 600, 296 counts with FWHM 95–300 cm⁻¹, i.e. unreliable.
observations.source: Ferrari & Robertson, Phys. Rev. B 61, 14095 (2000), three-stage model: I_D/I_G peaks and then falls as sp² clusters shrink; Cançado et al., Nano Lett. 11, 3190 (2011) for the stage-2 crossover near L_D ≈ 3 nm

observations.finding: Doses 1–3 show a single-layer-like 2D band with no detectable strain or doping change; the G position and 2D width are constant across these doses.
At dose 4 the G up-shift of ~11 cm⁻¹ is not accompanied by a comparable 2D shift, which points to disorder rather than pure charge doping, though this is not conclusive.
observations.evidence: ΔPos(G) ≈ +11.0 cm⁻¹ (1580.4 → 1591.4) while ΔPos(2D) ≈ +2.5 cm⁻¹ (2690 → 2692.4, with large uncertainty from the broad 2D fit). Doping would give a 2D shift of roughly 0.7× the G shift.
observations.source: Lee et al., Nat. Commun. 3, 1024 (2012) on separating strain from doping via the Pos(G)–Pos(2D) correlation (slope value as recalled)

observations.finding: I_D/I_D' is about 6.2 (dose 1, but D' is only 2.2σ above noise), 6.3 (dose 2) and 6.9 (dose 3), in the range associated with vacancy-like defects; dose 4 is not determinable.
observations.evidence: D' heights 114 ± 51, 326 ± 61, 430 ± 45 counts, giving I_D/I_D' = 6.2, 6.3 ± 1.2 and 6.9 ± 0.8. The dose-4 D' fit is degenerate with the broad G band (I_D/I_D' 14–19, not reliable).
observations.source: Eckmann et al., Nano Lett. 12, 3925 (2012): I_D/I_D' ≈ 13 for boundaries, ≈ 7 for vacancies, ≈ 3.5 for sp³ defects (values as recalled)

observations.finding: Instrument stability is good across doses 1–3: the G and 2D intensities normalised to the Si 520 cm⁻¹ reference are constant, so the absolute intensities can be compared even though the Si height itself varies by about 20%.
observations.evidence: Si peak heights 5691, 7242, 4920, 6542 counts; G/Si = 0.493, 0.496, 0.507, 0.489 (doses 1–4); 2D/Si = 1.49, 1.48, 1.50 (doses 1–3). Si position 520.9 cm⁻¹ vs the 520.7 cm⁻¹ reference, i.e. a ~+0.2 cm⁻¹ absolute offset; relative shifts are unaffected.

observations.finding: The dose-4 spectrum carries a broad elevated background between ~1100 and 2300 cm⁻¹ (about 1000 counts at 1250 cm⁻¹ versus ~700 for dose 1), which a linear baseline does not model.
observations.evidence: Binned median intensity in the 1100–1300 cm⁻¹ and 1600–1900 cm⁻¹ regions is about 1.5–2× the level of dose 1 for dose 4; the D-band fit residuals remain structured near the peak wings.

caveats: The absolute densities depend on the calibration. The graphene stage-1 relation (Cançado 2011) gives L_D ≈ 24/16/11 nm. The older graphite Tuinstra–Koenig form (L_a = 2.4e-10·λ⁴/(I_D/I_G), Cançado et al., APL 88, 163106 (2006)) gives L_a ≈ 77/34/16 nm for the same ratios. The trend across doses is robust; the absolute values can differ by a factor of ~2–4 between models.

I cited the Cançado 2011, Ferrari & Robertson 2000, Eckmann 2012, Lee 2012 and Lucchese 2010 coefficients and values from memory. I could not check them against the papers in this environment; verify the 1.8±0.5e-9 coefficient, the I_D/I_D' values and the stage-2 boundary before quoting numbers.

Dose-4 I_D/I_G (0.57) is numerically the same as dose 2 but physically the opposite situation. Applying the L_D formula to it would wrongly suggest a low defect density. Quote dose 4 as amorphized/strongly disordered, not as a defect density.
The dose-4 2D peak is effectively unresolved (height 236 ± 99 counts over a 600-count background; fit variants range 236–600). Its I_2D/I_G and any 2D-based strain/doping inference are unreliable.
D' is only 2.2σ above noise at dose 1 (114 ± 51 counts), so I_D/I_D' = 6.2 there is weak. Dose 2 and 3 values are better determined (± ~1 and ± ~0.8).

Uncertainties are fit-only (lmfit covariance; variant spread ≤0.004). If each dose is one spectrum from one spot, spot-to-spot heterogeneity on the flake is not included and may be larger than the fit errors.

The 1 mW, 532 nm laser could create defects itself. Check that the dose-0 / pristine reference is not affected by repeated measurement at this power before attributing all D-band growth to the dose treatment.
The Si reference sits at 520.9 cm⁻¹ instead of 520.7, so absolute Raman positions carry an offset of about +0.2 cm⁻¹. Relative shifts between doses are not affected.
The fits used Lorentzian peaks on a linear (or quadratic) baseline. The dose-4 background hump may bias the dose-4 D/G, so treat that ratio with extra caution.
questions_for_user: What is the 'dose' physically (ion, electron beam, plasma, laser exposure, chemical)? Without its units I can't convert the D/G trend into defects per unit dose or a cross-section.

Were all four spectra taken from the same spot, or from different spots on the flake? If different spots, is there spot-to-spot repeatability data? This determines whether the dose-1→3 trend is a real trend or flake heterogeneity.
Is there a dose-0 (pristine) reference spectrum from the same flake? That would set the zero of the defect density and check the 1 mW laser-damage concern.
Was the flake monolayer confirmed independently (optical contrast, AFM, or a second technique)? I inferred single-layer from the 2D shape and I_2D/I_G ≈ 3 only.
Was the broad elevated background at dose 4 (about 1100–2300 cm⁻¹) from resist/PMMA residue, amorphous carbon or substrate luminescence? The answer changes how much of the dose-4 D/G is intrinsic.
Is the calibration the same as in your lab's standard L_D formula? Please check the coefficients (1.8e-9 vs 2.4e-10 forms) against your reference before using absolute densities.
citations: Cançado, L. G. et al. Quantifying defects in graphene via Raman spectroscopy at different excitation energies. Nano Lett. 11, 3190 (2011) — stage-1 L_D and n_D relations (coefficient 1.8±0.5×10⁻⁹ λ⁴ as recalled); stage-2 crossover near L_D ≈ 3 nm; verify exact equations and figure.
Ferrari, A. C. & Robertson, J. Interpretation of Raman spectra of disordered and amorphous carbon. Phys. Rev. B 61, 14095 (2000) — three-stage model; I_D/I_G maximum and decrease with amorphization.

Cançado, L. G. et al. Measuring the degree of structural disorder in graphite / graphite-type materials. Appl. Phys. Lett. 88, 163106 (2006) — graphite L_a = 2.4e-10 λ⁴/(I_D/I_G), used as the alternative calibration.
Eckmann, A. et al. Probing the nature of defects in graphene by Raman spectroscopy. Nano Lett. 12, 3925 (2012) — I_D/I_D' ≈ 13 (boundary), ≈ 7 (vacancy), ≈ 3.5 (sp³) (values as recalled).
Lee, J. E. et al. Optical separation of mechanical strain from charge doping in graphene. Nat. Commun. 3, 1024 (2012) — Pos(G)–Pos(2D) correlation to separate strain from doping.
Lucchese, M. M. et al. Quantifying ion-induced defects and Raman relaxation length in graphene. Carbon 48, 1592 (2010) — original L_D² = 1.8e-9 λ⁴/(I_D/I_G) relation (as recalled).
limits: The data are one spectrum per dose with unknown dose units, so I cannot give defects per unit dose or a cross-section, only the trend in I_D/I_G and the derived L_D/n_D for doses 1–3.
Dose 4 is outside the range where any stage-1 L_D relation applies. I can say it is strongly disordered but cannot give a defect density for it.
Literature coefficients are from memory and were not checked against the papers in this environment. The numbers depend on which calibration is used.
The 2D peak at dose 4 is not resolved, so the 2D-based conclusions there (I_2D/I_G, 2D position, strain/doping) are unreliable.
No spot-to-spot or repeat-measurement statistics are available, so the reported uncertainties are fit-only.
Analysis scripts and the fit table (fit_table.csv) and diagnostic figure (diag_fits.png) are in C:/WINDOWS/TEMP/raman-analysis-scratch, outside the data folder; the data folder was not modified.
